$comment: SEED CATALOG - replace/extend with the real DOOH category list.
How a pack works (see detector.py for the maths):
positives  - phrases describing the thing we ARE hunting.
negatives  - HARD negatives: things that look confusably similar but are NOT the tag.
These do the real work. A protein tub and a baby-formula tub are nearly
identical photographs; without the negative, every formula tin reads as protein.
RULE 1: MIRROR THE PHRASINGS. If a positive says 'a scoop of protein powder',
a negative must say 'a scoop of <other thing>'. Measured: with only
'a tin of baby formula' as the negative, infant formula scored 0.709
(wrongly present). Adding 'a scoop of baby formula milk powder'
dropped it to 0.224 while real whey protein stayed at 0.999.
Asymmetric phrasing rigs the softmax toward whichever side owns
the words that describe the photo's composition.
RULE 2: Name the confusable NEIGHBOUR, not a random unrelated thing.
'a plain brick wall' as an alcohol negative teaches nothing;
'a bottle of fruit juice' is what actually gets mistaken for it.
thresholds - PROVISIONAL. Real values come from calibrate.py against labelled images.
Do not trust these numbers until calibration has run.
Adding a tag = editing this file. Never touch Python.

//sigmoid_floor: Weak backstop only -- NOT a primary gate. Measured on real photos:
true positives ranged 0.028 (beer) to 0.902 (cigarette), while true
negatives sat at 0.000. SigLIP's absolute sigmoid runs far lower than
you would guess, so a floor of 0.10 vetoes genuine detections.
The shared_distractors already absorb probability mass for unrelated
images, which is what keeps softmax honest. Leave this low.

tags.label: Alcoholic content
tags.description: Beer, wine, spirits, cocktails, bars, or drinking of alcohol.
positives: a glass of beer with foam
a cocktail glass with a lime garnish
a bar counter lined with liquor bottles
//negatives: The food entries are not padding. Calibration measured a photo of a
HAMBURGER at 0.939 for this tag — above champagne, cocktails, wine and
sake — because the positives describe bar and restaurant SCENES ('a bar
counter lined with liquor bottles', 'people toasting'), and pub food
matches that setting. One false positive that high forced the threshold
up and cut recall to 50%. Naming the scene explicitly as a negative is
what separates 'a bar' from 'food served in a bar'.
negatives: a hamburger and fries on a plate
a plate of restaurant food on a table
a pizza on a wooden board
a cafe table with pastries and coffee

tags.label: Protein and supplements
tags.description: Protein powder, whey tubs, shakers, supplement pills, protein bars.
positives: a protein shake in a shaker bottle
a whey protein container with a label
//negatives: MIRROR THE POSITIVES' PHRASINGS. The positives say 'a tub of' and 'a
scoop of', so the negatives must too. Originally the negatives only
offered 'a tin of baby formula milk powder' while the positives offered
'a scoop of protein powder' -- so a photo of a scoop of formula matched
the positive on the word 'scoop' alone and was called protein powder.
Asymmetric phrasing quietly rigs the softmax. Mirror it.
negatives: a tin of baby formula milk powder
a scoop of baby formula milk powder
a scoop of white milk powder
a baby bottle of formula milk

tags.label: Gambling and betting
tags.description: Casinos, betting, poker, slot machines, lottery.
positives: casino poker chips stacked on a table
a hand of playing cards being gambled
a sports betting app on a phone screen
dice being thrown on a casino table
//negatives: The last four are not padding either, and they are the ones that matter for DOOH.
Measured: a portrait 'BIG SALE OFFER' poster — a model on flat orange under huge
display type — scored 0.6167 for this tag on 'a sports betting app on a phone
screen', which is PRESENT under threshold_high 0.55, and a real advertiser was
refused over it. Nothing in the pool described what every DOOH creative actually
is: a designed advertisement. The board games and machines above are all PHYSICAL
objects, so a bright rectangular panel covered in lettering had nowhere to land
except the betting-app prompt.
RULE 1 in force: each mirrors a positive's composition rather than its subject.
'a sports betting app on a phone screen' now has 'a shopping app...' and 'a sale
advertisement on a phone screen' opposite it, and the two poster phrases cover the
designed-artwork case the whole catalog was missing.
Result on the same poster: 0.6167 -> 0.0377, decided by the SCORE and not by the
sigmoid floor, which matters — the floor had been the only thing holding this back
and it was doing so by 0.0132 against 0.005. Real gambling is untouched: slot
machine 0.9964, casino chips 0.9996, roulette 0.9999. Guarded by smoke_test.py.
negatives: a family playing a board game
a shopping app on a phone screen
a sale advertisement on a phone screen
an advertising poster with large bold text
a retail sale poster with big discount lettering
